title: Styles
grade_reasons: The steward's C stands. The base is sound: hand-written CSS has almost no dead weight, a built page carries under 5 KB of inline style, the admin's own CSS is a file apart, and style generation and fonts are cached. But the one render-blocking sheet every shopper loads is 28% the admin's (183,124 bytes raw / 25,832 Brotli, re-measured on the build's file; 129,745 / 19,762 when the site's entry is compiled alone), a fixed sheet is copied once per row and a third time per document, and not one test or figure holds the sheet's size, its sources or the style text. It is not a D, because no page carries far more than its job needs, and not a B, because no budget exists. The main button of /status and /report has no fill (seen again in the built HTML and CSS): a fault, not waste, so it does not make an E.
verdict_on_bar: KEPT, after checking the floor. The stylesheet bar of 135,000 bytes raw / 20,600 Brotli: I parsed the compiled site sheet. Tailwind's fixed layers are 13.0 KB, hand-written site CSS 28.4 KB, motion.css 18.7 KB and utilities 69.6 KB, and the largest utility rules are ordinary ones (two @media blocks, backdrop-blur, transition, the rings). There is no fat to ask for inside a one-sheet design. Also kept: 0 outside files that can rename the sheet; 2 copies of a sheet per document (Kaizena Flow's front page, which draws its layout once, already shows 2, so that is the framework's floor for an inline sheet); 0 colours without a value; 0 admin fetches from public pages; and the admin's 208,000. The admin cannot load 'its own classes plus the site's sheet': two Tailwind sheets on one document put the same class in both, and the later sheet's plain class then beats the earlier sheet's md: class. So the admin's entry must read what the canvas draws, and 49 KB raw of storefront CSS on plain admin screens is a fair tolerance. TIGHTENED. (1) The tolerance is now a measure of its own with failing lines. After the split a shopper of a launch-theme store still gets about 5 KB Brotli, a quarter of the sheet, that the page cannot use: motion.css 3.4 KB (measured by removing it from the compiled sheet) and 1.5 KB of classes only Kaizena Flow's pages or the on-site editor name. That is as much as the admin's share the split removes (5.6 KB). I accept it as the stated tolerance because it is about 1% of a first visit's bytes, but only held: step 1.23's script must fail above the line, not merely run. (2) motion.css is tolerated on a condition with numbers, and the step that follows is written now. (3) Brotli is held in the spec beside raw bytes. (4) The launch-theme store's measure gets numbers: at most 3 render-blocking stylesheets, and at most 35 KB raw of style text on Orbit's home (about 62 KB today, about 31 KB after steps 2.2 and 2.3, computed with the real functions). (5) The owners' style text is marked per store above 20 KB, not read as a median only: one store at the cap puts 300 KB of CSS into every document. (6) The colour bar says light and dark, and that a test holds it; the plan's step proves two buttons once. LOOSENED. The raw line for platform-only and editor-only classes goes from 15 KB to 17 KB. Two honest counts differ on which pages are the platform's: the steward's 13.8 KB and mine 16.2 KB (rules removed from the compiled sheet). Both give 1.5 to 1.6 KB Brotli, so the Brotli line of 2.0 KB is the one that binds, and the script must fix one definition by root layout. MERGED. The prefetch of /admin is now part of the admin's measure. NOT USED. Chromium's CSS coverage: it reports about 127 KB of the sheet as used on every page, the admin's sign-in included, so it cannot be a measure here.

measures.name: The stylesheet a shopper's browser loads before a store page paints
measures.today: 183,124 bytes raw / 25,832 Brotli (32,018 gzip): one file for stores, Kaizena Flow's site, the docs and the admin. Nothing holds it: the page-weight budget is 450,000 bytes for pages of 311 to 331 KB.
measures.target_a: At most 135,000 bytes raw and 20,600 Brotli, both held. The site's entry compiled alone gives 129,745 / 19,762. The build writes today's sheet 1,538 bytes raw and 472 Brotli above the same compile, and step 0.34 adds about 400 bytes, so expect about 131,700 / 20,300. The budget in the spec is the first built figure plus 3%, never above the bar, and it only falls.
measures.how_measured: STYLESHEET_BUDGETS in e2e/performance.spec.ts (step 1.3 makes it; it does not exist today): raw bytes and node zlib Brotli of the /_next/static stylesheets that the HTML of /s/demo/no and of / links, printed with E2E_MEASURE=1. Step 2.11 lowers it to the bar.

measures.name: What is in that stylesheet that a store's shopper cannot use
measures.today: Three parts, none counted by anything. (1) 51.8 KB raw / 5.6 KB Brotli that only admin screens, tests or the builder's canvas name. (2) 13.8 to 16.2 KB raw / 1.5 to 1.6 KB Brotli that only Kaizena Flow's own pages or the staff's on-site editor name (the steward's count and the challenger's, which differ on which pages are the platform's). (3) motion.css: 18.7 KB raw, 3.4 KB Brotli inside the sheet. A store on one of the six launch themes does not use it until its owner adds a builder effect.
measures.target_a: (1) 0, except the classes of the listed admin parts a public page draws (45 classes, 3.0 KB). (2) At most 2.0 KB Brotli and 17 KB raw, failing above; a third stylesheet for stores is weighed only above it. (3) motion.css stays in the sheet only while the reading says at least half of published store pages use it. Under half, it is loaded where a page uses it, and the bar of the first measure falls to 116,500 raw / 17,400 Brotli.
measures.how_measured: docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/scripts/stylesheet-audiences.mjs on CI's build (step 1.23 makes it). It must decide an audience by which root layouts reach the file that names a class, and exit non-zero above a line: the step asks only that it runs. The motion share is the line on Platform, Usage and limits of the same step.

measures.name: Files that can rename the shoppers' stylesheet though no public page draws them
measures.today: 3,480 of the 5,931 files Tailwind reads: both admin folders, tests, message files, src/db and the migrations' SQL (src/app/globals.css lines 7 to 9). In 115 sampled commits, 13 added a class and 6 of those touched only admin folders or tests.
measures.target_a: 0. The site's entry reads the site's code (2,451 files) and each admin part a public page imports, named on a line of its own (11 files today). The test fails both ways: for a source no public page reaches, and for an admin part a public page imports that has no line.
measures.how_measured: src/lib/stylesheet-sources.scan.test.ts (step 0.35 makes it, step 2.11 finishes it): it reads each entry's @source lines and walks imports from every public page. CI's run summary prints the site sheet's file name, so renames per week can be read (a proposed change).

measures.name: Copies of one style sheet in a store document
measures.today: 3 plus one per row: the 1,760-byte breakpoint sheet is 4 times in the demo's one-row front page and the theme's sheet 3 times (counted in m/html/store-home.html). Kaizena Flow's front page has 2. On Orbit's home (6 rows, its header and footer) about 62 KB raw of style text, computed with the real functions, not seen in a browser.
measures.target_a: 2 of each sheet, whatever the number of rows: once in the HTML and once in the payload Next sends with it. On Orbit's home at most 35 KB raw of style text (about 31 KB computed, with one sheet for a page's rows).
measures.how_measured: The count of the hrefs kz-bp- and theme- in the served HTML of a three-row test page (e2e/performance.spec.ts, step 2.3) and of the launch-theme store's home (step 1.6), with the bytes of all style elements and of the same text in the payload.

measures.name: Classes on public pages that read a colour with no value there
measures.today: 145 uses of 13 admin colour names: 20 in seven shop and site files, 125 in eleven admin parts that public pages draw. Checked again in the build: the submit button of /status has class bg-brand, its page has no data-admin, and only the admin's sheet sets --brand. The same button is on /report, the sign-up confirm page, /get-domain and every hosted invoice.
measures.target_a: 0, in light and in dark, and it cannot come back: a shop file that names an admin colour fails a test, and so does a colour the shared admin parts read that has no value outside the admin.
measures.how_measured: Two rules in src/lib/stylesheet-sources.scan.test.ts, and a computed-colour check on /report, /status and a hosted invoice in e2e. Step 0.34 asks only for the check on the two buttons: the two rules, dark and the invoice are a proposed change.

measures.name: The admin's stylesheets: on admin screens, and on public pages
measures.today: 204,207 bytes raw / 29.3 KB Brotli on every admin screen, sign-in included (the shared sheet and the admin's own 21,083), held by nothing. Kaizena Flow's front page, a blog post and the theme store each fetch the admin's sheet and two /admin answers after load: 12.2 KB and 3 requests (m/routes.json).
measures.target_a: At most 208,000 bytes raw on an admin screen, held by a budget that only falls (about 204,000 expected after the split). 0 admin stylesheets and 0 /admin answers fetched by a public page.
measures.how_measured: STYLESHEET_BUDGETS for /admin/sign-in in e2e/performance.spec.ts (step 1.3). e2e/prefetch.spec.ts (step 0.12): no request to /admin after loading /, and no stylesheet fetched that the HTML did not link.

measures.name: A launch-theme store's styles under a budget
measures.today: None. All 12 measured store pages are the bare demo store: one row, no theme CSS, 0 font stylesheets. A launch theme links one render-blocking stylesheet per font family, so a real store's first paint waits for three, two of them never measured. Production's front page showed 38 KB of CSS on the wire on 5 November (docs/performance.md) against 25.8 KB for the one sheet, and nobody has split out the rest.
measures.target_a: The seeded Orbit store's home holds: at most 3 render-blocking stylesheets (the site's and one per font family) with the bytes of each, the style text of the copies measure, and 2 copies of each sheet. Each figure is held within 5% of its first reading and lowered by steps 2.2 and 2.3.
measures.how_measured: e2e/performance.spec.ts on the themed store of step 1.6, and the same pages in docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/scripts/measure-routes.mjs.

measures.name: Style text owners add to every document
measures.today: No figure. An owner's CSS is capped at 50,000 characters a sheet (src/lib/custom-css.ts:19). The layout writes the store's, the header's and the footer's into every document (src/app/s/[store]/[market]/layout.tsx:168-170), three times today: up to 450 KB raw, 300 KB after step 2.2. The launch themes' own layout-level sheets are 6.6 to 9.5 KB, just under the 10 KB line.
measures.target_a: A figure per store on Platform, Usage and limits, read before opening and each quarter: bytes of layout-level CSS, with a mark on any store above 20 KB. Two written lines: the median store above 10 KB, or any store above 20 KB, and that CSS moves to an external hashed sheet.
measures.how_measured: The line on Platform, Usage and limits and the first reading of the team's 60 stores in docs/performance.md (step 1.23). The per-store mark is a proposed change.

bar_in_a_sentence: A shopper's browser loads one stylesheet of at most 135 KB (20.6 KB compressed) with nothing in it that only the admin uses, a store's document carries each style sheet twice and no more, and every colour a public page reads has a value. A test fails, or a figure on the platform's own screen shows it, when any of this slips.
can_the_steps_reach_a: The values: yes, at the end of phase 2. The holds: not as written. THE SUMS. Stylesheet: 183,124 raw / 25,832 Brotli. Step 0.35 takes 436 bytes and 0.34 adds about 400. Step 2.11 takes 51.8 KB raw / 5.6 KB Brotli: 129,745 / 19,762 compiled, about 131,700 / 20,300 in the build. That is under 135,000 / 20,600 with 2.5% and 1.5% to spare. Sources: 3,480 files, 1,533 after 0.35, 0 after 2.11. Copies: 3 plus one per row, 2 plus one per row after 2.2, 2 after 2.3; Orbit's home about 62 KB of style text to about 31 KB. Colours: 145 to 0 in step 0.34. Admin: 204,207 to about 204,000, under 208,000; its leak to public pages 12.2 KB to 0 in step 0.12. The themed store and the owners' figure exist after steps 1.6 and 1.23. WHERE IT STOPS SHORT. (1) Step 0.34 proves two buttons once; nothing stops the 146th use. (2) Step 1.23's script runs but fails nothing, and its 15 KB line is already passed by one honest count (16.2 KB). (3) Step 1.23 reads the median store only, and its trigger for motion.css names no step to build. (4) Six done-whens say less than the bar: no Brotli, no style-text figure, no both-way source test. As written the area ends a B: every value is at the bar, three measures have no check. With the four changes below it is an A at the end of phase 2. The ladder assumes them. ONE ORDER. Step 2.11 comes after step 1.21: the build has 0.8 GB of room on its 8 GB machine and was killed once on 11 November, and the finding's own way back (keep one sheet if the peak rises more than 150 MB) would leave the first three measures short for good.

shortfalls.what: The colour measure has a value after step 0.34 but no hold. The step's done-when is an rg count taken once and an e2e check of two buttons in light. The other 143 uses, dark, the hosted invoice and any new use are held by nothing. After step 2.11 a miss is silent: a shop file that names an admin colour gets a class with no value.
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: Step 0.34, done-when tightened: hold the admin's colour names with two scan rules, in light and in dark
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: Add two rules to src/lib/stylesheet-sources.scan.test.ts in the same change. One: no file outside the two admin folders names an admin colour class, except the admin parts a public page imports. Two: every colour those parts name has a value in the site's block under html:not([data-admin]), once for light and once for dark. Add a hosted invoice to the computed-colour check.
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: Both rules pass in CI, and each fails when tried: border-line added to a shop file fails the first, a colour removed from the block fails the second. The e2e check reads a filled submit button on /report, /status and a hosted invoice, in light and in dark.

shortfalls.what: The tolerance for classes no store page can draw is a sentence in a doc and a script that 'runs on CI's build'. Nothing fails above it. Its 15 KB raw line is passed today by one of two honest counts (13.8 KB and 16.2 KB), because 'the platform's pages' is not defined. Nothing reports how often the shoppers' sheet is renamed.
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: Step 1.23, done-when tightened: the audiences script fails above its lines, with one definition
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: stylesheet-audiences.mjs decides a class's audience by which root layouts can reach the file that names it (the import walk of the sources test), not by folder names. It measures the share in the sheet: the sheet's Brotli and raw size with and without those rules. It exits non-zero when a class only admin files name is in the site's sheet (from step 2.11 on), or when platform-only and editor-only classes pass 2.0 KB Brotli or 17 KB raw. It prints the site sheet's file name into CI's run summary.
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: A trial build over either line turns CI's run red. docs/performance.md holds the definition and the first figure (1.5 to 1.6 KB Brotli today). The run summary of step 1.20 lists the site sheet's file name.

shortfalls.what: The owners' style text is read as a median with a 10 KB line. One store at the cap puts 150,000 characters of own CSS into every document, twice, and hides behind a healthy median. The steward asked for a decision on capping the sum of a store's sheets; the plan dropped it.
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: Step 1.23, one line added: mark any store whose own style text is large
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: The line on Platform, Usage and limits shows each store's layout-level style text and marks a store above 20 KB (40 KB raw in every full page load). docs/performance.md gains a third trigger line: any store above 20 KB, and that store's sheets move to one external hashed stylesheet. Record the owner's answer on whether the 50,000-character limit is per sheet or on the sum.
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: A test store with 25 KB of own CSS shows the mark on Usage and limits. docs/performance.md holds the three trigger lines, the first reading of the 60 stores and the decision on the limit.

shortfalls.what: motion.css is 3.4 KB Brotli, a sixth of the site's sheet, and no launch theme uses it. Step 1.23 writes 'under half of pages need it: build CS-2', but no step exists to build, and it does not say whether the team's 60 demo stores count as a reading. If the first reading that counts says under half, the area is a B with no step.
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: New step, built only when the reading says so: load motion.css where a page uses it
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: The reading that counts is the first one after a quarter of real stores; the demo stores' figure is written down but decides nothing, unless the owner asks for the step before opening. If under half of published store pages need it: a prebuild step writes motion.css under a hashed name, MotionSupport links it when the page, header or footer needs it (builder motion, a gradient background, background layers or split text), the site's entry drops the import and the admin's keeps it. A test ties every [data-fx-*] selector of the file to a code path that sets the flag.
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: A store page without builder motion links no motion stylesheet, the site's sheet is at most 116,500 bytes raw and 17,400 Brotli with its budget lowered, the gate test passes, and e2e/motion.spec.ts and e2e/animation.spec.ts pass.

shortfalls.what: Six done-whens say less than the bar. 1.3 names stylesheet budgets but not Brotli, the inline-style budget or the count of copies. 1.6 counts stylesheets but not their bytes. 2.3 has no figure for style text. 2.11 tests sources one way and does not say it follows 1.21. 0.35 does not say message files and src/db are out. 0.12 checks / only for requests, not stylesheets.
shortfalls.proposed_step_title: Steps 0.12, 0.35, 1.3, 1.6, 2.3 and 2.11: done-whens brought up to the bar
shortfalls.proposed_step_what: No new work, only stronger proofs. 0.12: no stylesheet is fetched after load that the HTML did not link, on every page of the prefetch table. 0.35: Tailwind reads 3,984 files (5,931 today), with message files and src/db out too. 1.3: the stylesheet budgets hold raw and Brotli; the store home's style text is at most 6,000 bytes and the breakpoint sheet's href at most 4 times. 1.6: the themed home holds the bytes of each linked stylesheet, the two font sheets included. 2.3: Orbit's home holds at most 35 KB raw of style text. 2.11: it follows step 1.21, and the sources test fails for an admin part a public page imports that has no line, as well as for a line no public page reaches.
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: Each of the six done-whens carries its sentence above, and the spec prints every figure with E2E_MEASURE=1.

tolerated: motion.css stays in every store's stylesheet: 18.7 KB raw, 3.4 KB compressed, also for a store with no builder motion. It stays while at least half of published store pages use it. Loading it apart costs a build step and one more blocking request on pages that do use it (CS-2).

Classes that only Kaizena Flow's own pages or the staff's on-site editor use sit in every store's stylesheet: at most 17 KB raw and 2 KB compressed (1.5 KB today). A third stylesheet for stores would save a shopper about 1.1 KB compressed.

Plain admin screens carry about 49 KB raw of storefront and motion styles. The builder's canvas and the previews draw the storefront inside the admin, and two Tailwind sheets on one page cannot be ordered safely. It is one cached file for a signed-in owner.
Each inline style sheet is in a document twice, once as HTML and once in the payload Next sends with it. That is the framework's floor. On Orbit's home it is about 31 KB raw.

A store's layout-level CSS stays inline in the document, not in a file of its own, while the median store is under 10 KB and no store is over 20 KB. An external sheet would add a blocking request to every first visit.
A themed store's first paint waits for three stylesheets: the site's and one per font family. They are asked for together on one connection.
Each dark utility is written twice, by attribute and by the device's setting: 3.4 KB raw, 0.17 KB compressed. It lets a page be dark without scripts.
Both admin colour schemes are in one file: the one not in use costs 0.44 KB compressed.
About 2.5% of room between the expected stylesheet and its bar. A person who visits Kaizena Flow's site and then signs in downloads two full sheets once.
owner_choices: Step 2.11: after the split, a Tailwind class typed in a part's Advanced tab can show on the builder's canvas and not on the live site. Is it enough to say in the docs that only classes styled by the owner's own CSS are promised, or should the site's stylesheet keep a short fixed list of utility names owners may type?

Motion styles are 3.4 KB compressed, a sixth of the stylesheet, and reach every store's first visit. A store started from a launch theme does not use them until its owner adds a builder effect. Loading them only where used is a medium step with one risk: a missed case breaks a background. The plan waits for the first quarter's figures from real stores. Do you want it built before opening instead? Either way the area can be an A; waiting means the A rests on that reading.

An owner's own CSS is limited to 50,000 characters for each of three sheets (the store's, the header's, the footer's), and all three go into every document. Should the limit be on the sum? No real store is affected today.
